title: Investigating the Effectiveness of the Biopsychosocial Model-Based Exercise Approach in Children and Adults Diagnosed With Scleroderma
off: Investigating the Effectiveness of the Biopsychosocial Model-Based Exercise Approach (BETY) in Children and Adults Diagnosed With Scleroderma: A Single-Blind Randomized Controlled Trial
summary: This study aims to investigate the effectiveness of BETY, an exercise approach based on the biopsychosocial model, in children and adults diagnosed with scleroderma.
desc:
EULAR recommendations on non-pharmacological treatment of scleroderma emphasize physical activity and patient education, disease-specific, evidence-based management strategies tailored to the individual, and self-management. Physical exercise is the most widely studied disease management strategy in scleroderma.

There is a reported need for biopsychosocial treatment approaches in disease management for cases and individuals diagnosed with scleroderma; therefore, the use of biopsychosocial approaches in the field of exercise is also recommended.

The Cognitive Exercise Therapy Approach (BETY), an innovative exercise approach developed for adults diagnosed with rheumatic diseases, also aims to promote behavioral change through exercises that provide pain management and functional gains in pediatric rheumatology, and to prevent social isolation through group support. As in adults, there is a need for exercise approaches, such as BETY, that align with the biopsychosocial model in pediatric cases.

BETY, previously implemented via telerehabilitation in individuals diagnosed with systemic sclerosis, has been shown to have beneficial effects on functionality, muscle strength, vascular structures, inflammatory markers, and biopsychosocial status.

In this context, there is a clear need for interventions that support both children and adults diagnosed with scleroderma physically and psychosocially. This study aims to investigate the effectiveness of BETY, an exercise approach based on the biopsychosocial model, in children and adults diagnosed with scleroderma.
elig:
\*For a child diagnosed with scleroderma\*

Inclusion Criteria:

* Cases diagnosed with scleroderma,
* Cases aged 7-18 years will be included.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Advanced heart/lung/liver/kidney disease, neurological disease, and malignancies
* Cases that are not willing to participate in the study will be excluded.
* History of developmental delay
* Having participated in a regular exercise program for the past 3 months
* Individuals who are not willing to participate in the study

\*For adults diagnosed with scleroderma\*

Inclusion Criteria:

* Individuals diagnosed with scleroderma,
* Individuals over the age of 18 will be included.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Advanced heart/lung/liver/kidney disease, neurological disease, and malignancies
* Individuals who are not willing to participate in the study will be excluded.
* Having participated in a regular exercise program for the past 3 months
* Individuals who are not willing to participate in the study

arms.d: Children and adults with scleroderma are participating in BETY sessions two times a week for 3 months.
Children and adults with scleroderma are followed up with a home exercise program.

x.titre: Exercice biopsychosocial (BETY) dans la sclérodermie de l'enfant et de l'adulte
x.question: Un programme d'exercice biopsychosocial supervisé améliore-t-il l'état des enfants et adultes atteints de sclérodermie par rapport à un programme à domicile ?
x.contexte:
La sclérodermie (systémique ou localisée) retentit sur la peau, la mobilité, la fonction et le vécu psychosocial. Les recommandations de l'EULAR sur les traitements non médicamenteux insistent sur l'activité physique, l'éducation et l'autogestion adaptées à chaque patient.

L'exercice est la stratégie non médicamenteuse la plus étudiée dans la sclérodermie, et des approches biopsychosociales sont recommandées. L'approche cognitive d'exercice thérapeutique (BETY), développée chez l'adulte rhumatisant, vise un changement de comportement, la gestion de la douleur gagnée en fonction et le soutien de groupe contre l'isolement. Elle a déjà été testée en téléréadaptation dans la sclérodermie systémique, avec des effets favorables sur la fonction, la force musculaire, la vascularisation et l'inflammation.

Cette étude randomisée de l'Université Hacettepe (Turquie) l'évalue chez 48 enfants (7-18 ans) et adultes, deux séances par semaine pendant 3 mois, contre un programme d'exercices à domicile.
x.interet: Elle pourrait étayer une rééducation structurée, y compris en pédiatrie, dans une maladie où les options non médicamenteuses sont peu validées. Critères multiples, effectif modeste, essai non en aveugle probable.
x.profil: Des enfants de 7 à 18 ans et des adultes atteints de sclérodermie.
inclusion: Enfants de 7 à 18 ans, ou adultes de plus de 18 ans
exclusion: Maladie cardiaque, pulmonaire, hépatique ou rénale avancée
Programme d'exercice régulier dans les 3 derniers mois

bras.traitement: Séances d'approche cognitive d'exercice thérapeutique, 2 fois par semaine pendant 3 mois

x.critere: Échelles biopsychosociales (JAB-Q, BETY-BQ), score cutané de Rodnan modifié, LoSCAT et test de marche de 6 minutes à 6 mois
